title: Reading Drill — Preserving handwritten menus — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Preserving handwritten menus — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The museum volunteer had been asked to investigate faint prices being confused with later corrections in Hillswick. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the rate of agreement between readers, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a six-week comparison, the team used enlarged scans at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because stains on the paper might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward paired transcription. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
